title: Fabrication of Human Skin Equivalents Using Decellularized Extracellular Matrix
author: Sarmin, Connelly

steps.title: Collect and prepare pig skin
steps.instruction: Obtain 50–100 g (≈20 × 10 cm) porcine belly skin from a local butcher, trim to manageable pieces and keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Prepare Dispase II stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve Dispase II powder in buffer containing 10 mM NaAc (pH 7.5) and 5 mM CaCl₂ to a concentration of 50 U ml⁻¹; filter‑sterilize and keep fresh.

steps.title: Dilute Dispase to working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the 50 U ml⁻¹ Dispase stock with sterile water to a final activity of 560 U L⁻¹ (0.56 U ml⁻¹) and use immediately.

steps.title: Remove epidermis with Dispase
steps.instruction: Incubate the skin pieces in the 560 U L⁻¹ Dispase solution at 37 °C until the epidermis separates, then peel off and discard the epidermal layer.

steps.title: Prepare Trypsin‑Triton solution
steps.instruction: Mix 1 % (v/v) Triton X‑100, 0.25 % (w/v) EDTA, and 0.69 % (w/v) Tris in sterile water; keep the solution fresh.

steps.title: Decellularize dermis
steps.instruction: Immerse the epidermis‑removed dermal tissue in the Trypsin/Triton solution at 37 °C with gentle agitation for the time required to remove cellular material, then rinse thoroughly with PBS.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry decellularized tissue
steps.instruction: Place the decellularized dermis in a −80 °C freezer overnight, then lyophilize in a lyophilizer until completely dry (low pressure and temperature maintained).

steps.title: Prepare pepsin solubilization solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 600 ml of 0.01 M HCl (diluted from concentrated stock) and dissolve 600 mg pepsin A; filter‑sterilize and use fresh.

steps.title: Solubilize freeze‑dried ECM
steps.instruction: Add the freeze‑dried ECM to the pepsin solution, stir at room temperature until fully dissolved, yielding a 20 mg ml⁻¹ dECM solution (≈500 ml expected from 50–100 g skin).

steps.title: Aliquot and store dECM
steps.instruction: Dispense the 20 mg ml⁻¹ dECM into sterile small aliquots and store at −20 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Neutralize dECM for cell embedding
steps.instruction: On ice, neutralize the acidic dECM by adding sterile 1 N NaOH dropwise while mixing, then bring the pH to ~7.4 with sterile PBS, producing neutralized dECM ready for cell embedding.

steps.title: Prepare FAD culture medium
steps.instruction: Combine 250 ml DMEM, 250 ml DMEM/F12 (1:1), 10 % v/v FBS, and 1 % v/v Pen/Strep; supplement with 10⁻¹⁰ M cholera toxin, 0.5 µg ml⁻¹ hydrocortisone, 10 ng ml⁻¹ EGF, and 50 µg ml⁻¹ insulin. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Embed fibroblasts in dECM gel
steps.instruction: Mix primary human dermal fibroblasts (neonatal) with the neutralized dECM to the desired cell density, then pipette equal volumes into each 0.4 mm PTFE transwell insert (12‑well plate), avoiding bubbles.

steps.title: Gel polymerization
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ~30 minutes (or until the dECM forms a soft gel).

steps.title: Seed keratinocytes on gel
steps.instruction: Add primary (or immortalized) human keratinocytes on top of the solidified dECM at the appropriate density.

steps.title: Air‑liquid interface culture
steps.instruction: Add FAD medium to the lower well so that the bottom of each transwell contacts medium while the surface of the construct remains dry; maintain at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 14 days, changing medium every 2–3 days and ensuring no medium contacts the epidermal surface.

steps.title: Harvest and analyze HSE
steps.instruction: After 14 days, fix the human skin equivalents and process for H&E staining and immunohistochemistry to assess epidermal differentiation and dermal contraction.

steps.title: Overall timeline
steps.instruction: The complete dECM preparation (decellularization, freeze‑drying, solubilization) requires approximately 7–10 days; construction of the HSE model takes one full day followed by 2 weeks of culture before analysis.
